In the lower left is a general ketone fragment, the carbonyl carbon is connected to R1 and R2, and the carbonyl oxygen is connected to Al; there are also mechanism arrows in the figure, but the question requires ignoring the arrows. In the lower right there is also an O-C(H)(CH3)2 isopropoxy fragment connected to Al. Reasoning: Starting from the general ketone carbon on the left according to the specified method, the two unknown substituents are represented by asterisks as *C(*). This carbon is connected to aluminum through oxygen, written as *C(*)O=[Al]. Three isopropoxy ligands are visible on aluminum: the two top-labeled i-PrO/Oi-Pr, and the right-side O-CH(CH3)2, each written as OC(C)C. Connecting these three OC(C)C ligands to Al gives the SMILES: *C(*)O=[Al](OC(C)C)(OC(C)C)OC(C)C.

method.method_draft: Read the molecule from the drawing rather than interpreting the mechanism arrows. Start with the left generic ketone carbon bearing two unknown substituents, giving *C(*). Attach its oxygen to aluminum as *C(*)O=[Al]. Then add the aluminum ligands visible in the image: two labeled top isopropoxy groups and the right O-CH(CH3)2 group, each written as OC(C)C. Combine these around aluminum to obtain *C(*)O=[Al](OC(C)C)(OC(C)C)OC(C)C.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中上方中心是 Al，Al 的左上和右上各连接一个标注为 i-PrO / Oi-Pr 的异丙氧基配体。左下方是一个通式酮片段，羰基碳连有 R1 和 R2，羰基氧与 Al 相连；图中还有机理箭头，但题目要求忽略箭头。右下方还有一个 O-C(H)(CH3)2 的异丙氧基片段与 Al 相连。
推理：按指定方法从左侧通式酮碳开始，两个未知取代基用星号表示为 *C(*)。该碳通过氧连接到铝，写作 *C(*)O=[Al]。铝上可见三个异丙氧基配体：两个顶部标注的 i-PrO/Oi-Pr，以及右侧的 O-CH(CH3)2，每个写作 OC(C)C。把这三个 OC(C)C 配体接到 Al 上，得到 SMILES：*C(*)O=[Al](OC(C)C)(OC(C)C)OC(C)C。

planner_metadata.image_role: Inspect the image first: note the central Al atom, two top ligands labeled i-PrO/Oi-Pr, a left carbonyl fragment with substituents R1 and R2 attached to its carbon, and a right isopropoxide-like O-C(H)(CH3)2 fragment coordinated to Al. Ignore the curved arrows as instructed and keep only atom connectivity.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know that the requested output is a SMILES expression and that the arrows in the transition-state diagram must be ignored.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use SMILES conventions: represent unspecified R groups by wildcard atoms '*'; write isopropoxy as OC(C)C; encode the carbonyl-derived fragment as *C(*)O attached to Al, with the depicted O-Al multiple/coordinate bond rendered as O=[Al] as in the accepted transition-state SMILES style; place the three isopropoxy groups as branches/ligands on Al.
